title: Incompatibility assisted Zeno-like confinement enables unbounded sharing of nonlocality
summary: To enable sequential sharing of Bell-nonlocality by an unbounded number of copies, each copy must satisfy two requirements. First, the measurements must be incompatible to extract nonlocality. Second, the post-processsed state, obtained as an equal mixture of the two post-measurement states, must remain nonlocal. We show that the incompatibility requirements impose nontrivial constraints on the choice of the initial nonlocal state and the amount of measurement noise required to ensure that the post-processed state remains nonlocal for an unbounded number of copies.
